So on the reduced space xt is x's conjugate at the string scale, while in the full zero-mode phase space the canonical pairs stay (p, x) and (pt, xt - pi alpha' p) (eq. 69). They call the (X,Y) units, with cell area hbar, 'the natural metastring parameterization', and the length-and-radius reading of (x, xt) 'deeply misleading' (sec. 7.1). The answer's 'a coordinate of a doubled space, conjugate (through qt) to winding' is right as structure. FLM's own reading is closer to the record's 'momentum side' than the answer allows. Also, 1812.10821 keeps x, xt non-Darboux by choice ('x,xt are preferred coordinates'), so whether xt counts as x's conjugate depends on the coordinates chosen. (3) The reader's leads call Chouha 2026 'probably not relevant'. But arXiv:2602.21407 (v1 2026-02-24, before the program's notebook) treats the metaparticle 'as a single entangled quantum object -- rather than as two independent sectors' and proposes a 'total entropy that incorporates correlations between the geometric and dual sectors' (abstract, code-checked). answers.question: Q9
answers.correction: Verified: no 'spontan', 'order parameter' or 'Goldstone' in any of the seven, and every 'potential' is a symplectic potential or unrelated, so there is no potential for eta. Four corrections. (a) 'The program's spontaneous reading ... has no counterpart here' is too strong. 1405.3949 sec. 2 says the bi-Lagrangian structure K, the space-momentum split, is not required by the formulation and is found 'when we look at solutions'; each string propagates on its own eta-null Lagrangian, and one spacetime for all strings arises only when eta is kinematical. My inference: this is a selection by solutions rather than by the action, which is the structure of spontaneous breaking, though without the word, a potential, an order parameter, or one vacuum for all matter. (b) Point (5)'s 'basis choice' omits 1606.01829 sec. 1.4, where the Stone-von Neumann theorem is 'fundamentally misleading' because polarizations differ in 'geometry, notions of regularity, and sets of C^infinity vectors'. (c) FLM say that in ordinary quantum mechanics 'this choice of polarization is immaterial' (1502.08005 sec. 1, the sentence before the one #11 sec. 3 quotes). They aim to restore the duality: 'a theory of quantum gravity ought to restore the kinematical duality principle' (1405.3949 sec. 1.1); 'These generalizations restore the Born duality symmetry' (1307.7080). (d) Supporting the answer: 1812.10821 sec. 1 leaves the localization mechanism open, and 1502.08005 sec. 2.3 keeps 'a preferred Lagrangian defined by the metastring fields'.

record_contradictions.record_says: review/wiki-build-flags.md item 64: 'In their foundations the dual coordinates are the canonical conjugate of x (Freidel, Leigh and Minic, Phys. Lett. B 730, 302 (2014): "so we will refer to Y as coordinates in momentum space")'; notes/literature-check.md sec. 3: 'the school's dual coordinates are the canonical conjugate of x'.
record_contradictions.note: Record wording checked: flag 64 and sec. 3 say this. The reader is right on three points. The cited sentence names Y for its period (p = loop integral of dY). FLM's canonically conjugate pairs are (p, x) and (pt, xt - pi alpha' p) (1706.03305 eq. 69; also 1502.08005 sec. 7.4, 'the momenta dual to x (resp. xt)', and 1707.00312 sec. 2, 'the conjugate operators P_A'). And xt is independent of p. But the reader's 'it is not the canonical conjugate of x' omits 1706.03305 sec. 4.2: 'xt/{2 pi lambda^2} plays the role of the variable conjugate to x', on the reduced (x, xt) space that the topological coupling makes 'a phase space'. It also omits that in 1307.7080 Y enters as the loop-space Fourier variable of X (d_sigma Y is X's momentum density). Flag 64 is therefore right for the reduced (x, xt) space, in a paper it does not cite. It is wrong for the full zero-mode phase space, where x's canonical partner is p, and the program's p stays a separate variable. My computation: hbar xt/(2 pi lambda^2) = xt/(pi alpha') = p + qt/(pi alpha'), with [x, qt] = 0, so xt's conjugacy to x comes from its p-content (verify_numbers.py B). The reader's 'contradicts the wording, qualifies the substance' should read: the wording has partial support, at the string scale, from a source the flag does not cite.

record_contradictions.record_says: notes/literature-check.md sec. 3: 'In the foundations it is the momentum side' ... 'In the model their dark-matter statements rest on, the metaparticle, the dual coordinate x̃ is a coordinate of a doubled phase space at the string scale, with [x, x̃] = iλ² ... their model doubles phase space where the program polarizes one.'
record_contradictions.note: The reader is right that the string foundations (1307.7080, 1502.08005, 1706.03305, 1707.00312) already work on the doubled (X, Y) beside (p, pt), so the doubling is not peculiar to the metaparticle. 1812.10821 itself says its symplectic form 'is again motivated by that of the zero modes of the Polyakov string'. The reader is also right that only 1606.01829 sets xt = p/epsilon. But 'momentum side' is FLM's own reading of the string foundations. Y 'can be thought of as a momentum coordinate', the dual theory is 'the Polyakov action for the momentum variable', and Lt is 'energy-momentum' (1502.08005 sec. 2). The (X,Y) units, with cell area hbar, are 'the natural metastring parameterization', and the length-and-radius reading of (x, xt) 'is deeply misleading' (sec. 7.1). On the coefficient, the reader's arithmetic is right (i lambda^2 needs lambda^2 = pi hbar alpha'), but it is not a contradiction. Hubsch and Minic 2024 (arXiv:2407.06207 sec. 3, full text read, code-checked) write the metaparticle Lagrangian with lambda^2 in place of 1812.10821's pi alpha', so the record quotes its source faithfully. That source calls lambda 'the contextuality parameter', not the string length. 'At the string scale' is the record's gloss, apt for 1706.03305 and 1707.00312, where lambda = sqrt(hbar alpha'/2).

record_contradictions.record_says: wiki/papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md sec. 3: 'They treat the breaking as kinematical and call the choice "a dynamical question".' wiki/phase-space/reciprocity/broken-born-duality.md: 'they wrote no potential for η and treated the breaking as kinematical, not as spontaneous symmetry breaking.'

Each describes the breaking by gravity, or eta in gravity; FLM's own proposal is that 'the purely kinematical splitting ... has to be made dynamical'. #11's sentence matches FLM's word for general relativity's breaking ('this kinematical breaking', 1405.3949 sec. 1.1), so it is incomplete rather than misquoted. record_contradictions.note: Verified: 1502.08005 sec. 2.1 credits dynamical eta to its ref. [3], which is 1307.7080 (reference list checked). 1307.7080 (v1 2013-07-26) says '(eta,J) ... dynamical'. 1405.3949 (v1 2014-05-15) says 'This is our addition to Born's argument [1]' ([1] = 1307.7080, checked) and 'There is a preferred basis — the space-time basis.' The reader's four points hold, and there is no spontaneous mechanism. Two corrections. (a) Point (4)'s 'not physical at all' overstates: 1606.01829 sec. 1.4 calls the Stone-von Neumann theorem 'fundamentally misleading in the present context' because 'different polarizations do have very different geometry, notions of regularity, and sets of C^infinity vectors'. record_contradictions.record_says: wiki/papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md sec. 5: 'Positive H satisfying both (η⁻¹H)² = 1 and (ω⁻¹H)² = −1 are exactly H = diag(g, g⁻¹), g ∈ Sym⁺(d)', attributed to Freidel, Leigh and Minic [26S, §2.1].
record_contradictions.note: Confirmed: 1502.08005 sec. 2.1 states the attributed sentence verbatim, for a Lorentzian H (fn. 9: signature (2,2(d-1)); eq. 14: h Lorentzian; 1307.7080: 'a generalized Lorentzian one'). Refuted: the reader's 'FLM did not state it for positive H; the positive-H version is the program's adaptation'. 1606.01829 sec. 2 gives GL(d) = Sp(2d) ∩ O(d,d) as the group 'determining the vacuum metric H(x,xt) = x q x + xt q^-1 xt', with q = e delta e^T positive, and says 'the space of vacuum metrics associated with a given Hilbert space is encoded in GL(d)/O(d)'. Its sec. 3 names 'a positive definite form H'. My code (verify_numbers.py E, gl_intersection.py) confirms three things. This H satisfies (eta^-1 H)^2 = 1 and (omega^-1 H)^2 = -1 with the paper's own eta (eq. 17) and omega (eq. 7). Sp(2d) ∩ O(d,d) = {diag(A, A^-T)}. Its orbit of H0 = 1 is diag(A^T A, (A^T A)^-1), which is diag(g, g^-1) with g in Sym+(d). FLM assert this in group form without proving the 'exactly' direction, so #11's block proof and machine check remain the program's. #11 sec. 5 could cite 1606.01829 sec. 2 for the positive form.
